note:
The household of Charles Ernest Bastow, ladies' mantle manufacturer, his wife Zella, their young niece and two servants at 3 Western Terrace (#342) on the 1911 return, transcribed by A. Hagues. 3 Western Terrace held only 1921, so 1911 is free, and none of the five was in the record.

Wright's Directory prints 'Bastow Charles Ernest, (mantle mfr)' at 3 Western Terrace in 1910-11 and 1913-14 - his census trade exactly, in the year of the census and three years after. He is gone from the 1915-16 volume, which prints no number 3 at all.

Florence Spencer, 13, is returned as their niece and was born at Coventry, so one of the Bastows had a sister or brother settled in Warwickshire; her parents are not on the schedule and no link is made beyond the niece relationship, which the importer cannot carry. She is not the Edith Spencer (#1115) or Gertrude Spencer (#2036) already in the record, both born much later. Ages are as the enumerator wrote them, so a birth year worked back from one may be a year out either way.
source: 1911 census, 3 Western Terrace, transcribed by A. Hagues. Directory evidence: Wright's Directory of Nottingham 1910-11 and 1913-14, Western Terrace number 3.
